mainTopic: A sloped סוכה with no separate roof (and רב יוסף's bridal canopy), and when a reed mat may be used as סכך
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: טיט הנרוק proves that something unfit by itself can still help something else become fit. Then a new משנה starts. A סוכה shaped like a sloped hut (צריף), or leaned against a wall, has no separate roof. רבי אליעזר says it is פסול, and the חכמים say it is כשר, because שיפועי אהלים כאהלים. אביי finds רב יוסף sleeping under a sloped bridal canopy in the סוכה and challenges him for following רבי אליעזר. רב יוסף answers that a ברייתא reverses the names, and that the משנה's version is only רבי נתן's. Another משנה teaches that a reed mat made for lying on is a כלי and cannot be סכך, while one made for roofing is valid. The גמרא finds a contradiction about a mat made with no stated purpose. רבא concludes that everyone agrees an unlabeled large mat is for roofing. For a small mat, the תנא קמא presumes it is for lying, and רבי אליעזר presumes it is for roofing.

steps.title: Liquid mortar proves that something unfit can still help make something else fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings טיט הנרוק as an example. It counts toward the forty סאה of a מקוה, yet a person cannot do טבילה in it alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Liquid mortar proves it. It combines with water to make up forty סאה, but someone who immerses in it alone has not done a valid טבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the previous discussion. It brings a proof that something can be unfit by itself and still help another thing become fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the question was whether anything exists that is not valid on its own but still counts toward making something else valid. טיט הנרוק is that kind of thing: it adds to the forty סאה of a מקוה, but you cannot do טבילה in mortar alone. This shows the idea is not strange, so the earlier claim can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Thin, pourable mortar or mud
Will prove it; a formula for bringing a proof from a known case
Combines; counts together toward a required amount
Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה
Ritual immersion

steps.whatToRemember: Something can count toward making another thing valid even if it could not be valid by itself. The example is טיט הנרוק in a מקוה.
steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the previous sugya, not to the new משנה that follows. Do not try to connect the mortar to the צריף case.

phrases.english: Pourable mortar will prove it,
phrases.notes: A proof from a known הלכה about מקוה

phrases.english: for it combines toward forty se'ah,
phrases.notes: It counts toward the minimum amount of a מקוה

phrases.aramaic: וְהַטּוֹבֵל בּוֹ — לֹא עָלְתָה לוֹ טְבִילָה.
phrases.english: yet one who immerses in it, his immersion is not valid.
phrases.notes: By itself, it cannot serve as a מקוה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion (on the previous amud) by bringing a proof case.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that something unfit by itself can still help another thing become fit
steps.raayaSupportSource: The הלכה of טיט הנרוק, which counts toward forty סאה of a מקוה but is not valid for טבילה alone

steps.title: A sloped hut or a סוכה leaned against a wall: the disagreement
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a סוכה shaped like a צריף, or leaned against a wall, is פסול according to רבי אליעזר because it has no roof. The חכמים say it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone made his סוכה like a sloped hut, or leaned it against a wall. רבי אליעזר says it is פסול because it has no roof. The חכמים say it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It presents a סוכה whose walls slope up and meet, so there is no separate flat roof, and it records a disagreement about whether such a סוכה is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the slanted branches act as both wall and roof at once. רבי אליעזר holds that a סוכה needs a roof you can tell apart from its walls, so he says it is פסול. The חכמים say it is כשר, and the גמרא will soon explain their reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Abbreviation for מתניתין, our משנה
Like a kind of hut whose walls slope up to a point, like an A-frame or cone
Leaned it against a wall, with one end on the ground and one end on the wall
Declares it invalid
Declare it valid

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר's problem is not that the סכך is bad material. His problem is that the shape has no roof that is separate from the walls.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
phrases.notes: Start of a new משנה

phrases.english: One who makes his sukkah like a kind of sloped hut,
phrases.notes: The walls slant up and meet at the top

phrases.english: or who leaned it against a wall —
phrases.notes: Slanted branches leaning on a wall

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer declares it invalid
because it has no roof,
phrases.notes: His reason is given in the משנה

phrases.english: and the Sages declare it valid.
phrases.notes: Their reason is not given here

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic and a new משנה, unrelated to the mortar proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sloped סוכה with no separate roof: רבי אליעזר says it is פסול, and the חכמים say it is כשר.

steps.title: When רבי אליעזר agrees the sloped סוכה is valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר agrees it is כשר if the סוכה is raised one טפח off the ground, or moved one טפח away from the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר agrees that if he raised it one טפח off the ground, or moved it one טפח away from the wall, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that narrows רבי אליעזר's opinion. It shows the cases where even he would say the סוכה is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raising the structure a טפח off the ground creates a short straight wall at the bottom (or the gap counts as a wall). Moving it a טפח from the wall creates a small roof area at the top. Either way, there is now a clear difference between wall and roof, so רבי אליעזר's objection that there is no roof goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes
He raised it
A handbreadth
He moved it away, distanced it

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי אליעזר does not reject sloped סכך itself. He only requires some visible distinction between roof and walls.

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא on this משנה

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer concedes
phrases.notes: A ברייתא

phrases.english: that if he raised it a handbreadth off the ground,
phrases.notes: Fixes the first case, the צריף

phrases.english: or he distanced it a handbreadth from the wall —
phrases.notes: Fixes the second case, the leaning סוכה

phrases.english: that it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי אליעזר's ruling from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a gap of one טפח from the ground or from the wall, even רבי אליעזר says the סוכה is כשר.

steps.title: What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים say a sloped סוכה with no flat roof is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the חכמים' view. The משנה gave רבי אליעזר's reason but not theirs, so this question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's reason is clear from the משנה: there is no roof. The חכמים seem to ignore that point. The גמרא wants to know how they handle it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reason?
The Sages, here the חכמים of the משנה

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: A request for their reasoning, not a challenge

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי אליעזר's view to the reasoning of the חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים accept a סוכה that has no roof separate from its walls.

steps.title: A sloping tent counts as a tent
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that the sloping sides of a tent have the same status as a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The slopes of tents are like tents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The חכמים hold that a slanted covering still counts as a real covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, a סוכה does not need a flat roof that stands out from the walls. A slanted covering still gives shelter, just like a tent, so it counts as the roof of the סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The slopes, slanting sides
Tents, coverings
Are similar to, have the same status as

steps.whatToRemember: The two views: רבי אליעזר requires a roof you can tell apart from the walls (unless there is a gap of a טפח). The חכמים say a slanted covering counts as a roof, because שיפועי אהלים כאהלים.

phrases.english: The slopes of tents
phrases.notes: Slanted coverings

phrases.english: are considered like tents.
phrases.notes: They have the full status of a covering

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The slopes of a tent count as a tent, so a slanted covering works as a roof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the חכמים, a סוכה shaped like a צריף or leaned against a wall is כשר, because a slanted covering has the status of a roof.

steps.title: אביי challenges רב יוסף for sleeping under a canopy in the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: אביי sees רב יוסף sleeping under a sloped bridal canopy in the סוכה. He asks: you must be following רבי אליעזר, so why did you leave the majority view of the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי found רב יוסף sleeping under a bridal canopy inside the סוכה. He said to him: Whose opinion are you following? רבי אליעזר's? You left the רבנן and acted like רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that puts the מחלוקת we just learned into real life. אביי challenges his teacher רב יוסף for seeming to follow the minority view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bridal canopy slopes down on all sides and has no flat roof, just like the צריף in our משנה. According to the חכמים, sloped sides count as a tent (Step 5). So the canopy is a 'tent inside the סוכה' that blocks the person from the סכך. Only רבי אליעזר, who says no roof means no tent, would allow sleeping under it, and normally we do not follow one opinion against the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: A bridal canopy: a netting that slopes down from a single point and has no flat roof
Sleeps / was sleeping
According to whom? (Whose opinion are you following?)
You abandoned / left
You acted / did

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the canopy itself. The problem is that, according to the חכמים, the canopy counts as its own tent. Sleeping under it would then be like sleeping under a roof inside the סוכה, not under the סכך.

phrases.english: Abaye found Rav Yosef
who was sleeping under a bridal canopy in the sukkah.
phrases.notes: The canopy slopes down and has no flat roof, like a צריף.

phrases.english: He said to him: Like whom? Like Rabbi Eliezer?
phrases.notes: Only רבי אליעזר holds that a structure with no roof is not a tent.

phrases.english: You abandoned the Rabbis
and acted like Rabbi Eliezer!
phrases.notes: The rule is to follow the majority against a single opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? שָׁבְקַתְּ רַבָּנַן וְעָבְדַתְּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the חכמים's reasoning (sloped sides count as a tent) to a real case and challenges רב יוסף's practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's practice of sleeping under a sloped canopy in the סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the חכמים, the sloped canopy is a tent that blocks the סכך. Only רבי אליעזר would allow it, and we do not follow one opinion against the majority.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a ברייתא reverses the opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that a ברייתא teaches the מחלוקת the other way around. There, רבי אליעזר is the one who validates the sloped structure and the חכמים invalidate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The ברייתא teaches the opposite: רבי אליעזר says it is valid, and the חכמים say it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself. He says he is actually following the majority, according to a different version of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's version, the חכמים are the ones who hold that a sloped structure is not a tent. That means sleeping under the canopy is fine according to the majority. So רב יוסף is not following a lone opinion at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
The opposite / reversed
Rules it valid
Rule it invalid

phrases.english: He said to him: The baraita teaches it the opposite way:
Rabbi Eliezer rules it valid, and the Sages rule it invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by offering a reversed version of the מחלוקת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף is following the minority opinion of רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the ברייתא, the majority (חכמים) hold that a sloped structure is not a tent, so the canopy does not block the סכך.

steps.title: אביי: Why follow a ברייתא over the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges again: the משנה is the more authoritative source. How can you leave it and follow a ברייתא?
steps.simpleTranslation: You abandoned the משנה and acted according to a ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's answer. He questions why a ברייתא should beat the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה was carefully edited and is usually treated as the main, reliable version. A ברייתא is less authoritative. So relying on the ברייתא's reversed names seems like the wrong choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה

phrases.english: You abandoned the Mishnah
and acted according to a baraita?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Relying on the ברייתא's version over the משנה's version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה is the authoritative, edited source. A ברייתא should not override it.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Our משנה is only an individual's version
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the version in our משנה reflects only one individual's report of the מחלוקת. It is not the majority's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our משנה is the view of a single individual.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why the ברייתא is more reliable here. The משנה's version comes from just one Sage. He will prove this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף is not saying the משנה is wrong in general. He is saying that this particular way of assigning the opinions comes from one person's tradition. Most Sages reported it the other way, as in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual / single opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree that there is a מחלוקת. The only question is WHO said WHAT, meaning which side holds that a sloped tent is a tent.

phrases.english: He said to him: Our Mishnah is an individual's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the authority of the משנה's version to a single Sage's tradition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's version represents the authoritative tradition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's version is one individual's report, so the majority's version in the ברייתא is followed.

steps.title: Proof: רבי נתן is the one who reports the משנה's version
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the משנה's version (רבי אליעזר invalidates, the חכמים validate) is reported in the name of רבי נתן alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One who makes his סוכה shaped like a צריף, or leans it against a wall, רבי נתן says: רבי אליעזר invalidates it because it has no roof, and the חכמים validate it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא to prove his claim that the משנה's version belongs to one individual. That individual is רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא presents the משנה's exact version with the words 'רבי נתן says.' This shows it is רבי נתן's personal report of the מחלוקת. So the reversed version is the majority tradition. Therefore the הלכה is that a sloped structure is not a tent, and sleeping under a canopy in the סוכה is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A cone or A-shaped hut whose walls slope up to a point
Roof

steps.whatToRemember: Two versions of the מחלוקת exist. The משנה's version is רבי נתן's alone. The majority's version is that the חכמים hold a roofless sloped structure is not a tent, so sleeping under a bridal canopy in the סוכה is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical basis for allowing a sloped canopy, net, or similar covering inside a סוכה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who makes his sukkah like a type of cone-shaped hut
or who leaned it against a wall,
Rabbi Natan says:
phrases.notes: The fact that it's רבי נתן saying this is the key to the proof.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פּוֹסֵל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ גַּג,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer invalidates it because it has no roof,
and the Sages validate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in Step 9 that the משנה reflects one individual's view.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה's version of the מחלוקת is only רבי נתן's report
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that attributes the משנה's version explicitly to רבי נתן

steps.title: New משנה: A large reed mat depends on what it was made for
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: whether a large reed mat may be used as סכך depends on its original purpose. If it was made for lying on, it is a כלי that can become טמא and may not be used as סכך. If it was made for roofing, it may be used as סכך and does not become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A large mat of reeds: if one made it for lying on, it can become טמא, and one may not use it as סכך. If one made it for roofing, one may use it as סכך, and it does not become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand new משנה begins, about using reed mats as סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סכך may not be something that can become טמא, and a כלי (utensil) can become טמא. A mat made for lying on is a כלי, so it is not allowed as סכך. A mat made for roofing is just building material, not a כלי, so it is allowed. This first opinion speaks about a large mat.

keyTerms.meaning: A mat woven from reeds
For lying on
Can become ritually impure (it has the status of a כלי)
May use it as סכך (roofing for a סוכה)
For roofing

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A large mat of reeds:
if one made it for lying on,
it can become impure, and one may not roof with it.
phrases.notes: Something that can become טמא is not valid as סכך.

phrases.english: If made for roofing, one may roof with it,
and it cannot become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic begins with a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A large reed mat made for lying on is a כלי and is not valid as סכך. One made for roofing is valid as סכך and is not susceptible to טומאה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Small or large, only the purpose matters
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the same rule applies to both small and large mats. The only thing that matters is what the mat was made for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Whether small or large, if one made it for lying on, it can become טמא and one may not use it as סכך. If one made it for roofing, one may use it as סכך and it does not become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי אליעזר's opinion. He extends the purpose-based rule to small mats as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion mentioned only a large mat, which suggests a small mat is treated differently. רבי אליעזר says size makes no difference: the maker's intended use decides the mat's status for every size. The גמרא later works out exactly where the two opinions differ (steps 19–20).

keyTerms.meaning: Both a small one and a large one

steps.whatToRemember: For reed mats, the key question is what the mat was made for (lying or roofing). רבי אליעזר applies this to all sizes, while the first opinion speaks only about a large mat.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַחַת קְטַנָּה וְאַחַת גְּדוֹלָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Both a small one and a large one:
if one made it for lying on, it can become impure
and one may not roof with it;
if made for roofing, one may roof with it,
and it cannot become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַחַת קְטַנָּה וְאַחַת גְּדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, broader opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For both small and large mats, the status depends only on the intended purpose: lying (a כלי, not valid as סכך) or roofing (valid as סכך, not susceptible to טומאה).

steps.title: The first half of the משנה implies an unlabeled mat is for roofing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces a contradiction inside the משנה. It starts by drawing an inference from the first clause: only a mat made for lying is invalid, so an unlabeled mat is valid for roofing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This משנה contradicts itself. You said: if one made it for lying on, it can become טמא and may not be used as סכך. The reason is that he made it for lying on. That implies a mat made with no stated purpose counts as made for roofing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge. It reads the first half of the משנה closely and draws an inference about a mat with no stated purpose. This is only the first side of the contradiction; the other side comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a mat 'made for lying' is invalid. Why mention a specific purpose unless it matters? So the גמרא infers that a mat with no stated purpose (סתמא) is treated as roofing and is valid as סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: This text itself is difficult; it contradicts itself
The reason is (used to draw an inference from a specific detail)
Unspecified; made with no stated purpose
Lying down (the mat was made to lie on)
Roofing a סוכה
Can become ritually impure (it is a כלי)

steps.confusionAlert: Nothing here is said outright in the משנה. The גמרא is drawing an inference from what the משנה chose to say (a 'דיוק'). The contradiction is between two inferences, not between two explicit rulings.

phrases.english: GEMARA: This itself is difficult.
You said: if one made it for lying on,
it can become impure, and one may not roof with it.
The reason is that he made it for lying on,
which implies that an unspecified mat is for roofing.
phrases.notes: First inference: an unlabeled mat is valid as סכך.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: דיוק (inference) serving as the first half of a קשיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the new משנה quoted in steps 11–12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the משנה about mats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause's wording implies that an unspecified mat is for roofing. This is the first half of a two-sided contradiction.

steps.title: The second half of the משנה implies an unlabeled mat is for lying
steps.stepSummary: The second clause says a mat made for roofing is valid. This implies an unlabeled mat is treated as made for lying, which contradicts the first inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And then the משנה teaches: if made for roofing, one may roof with it and it cannot become טמא. The reason is that he made it for roofing. That implies a mat made with no stated purpose counts as made for lying on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. It draws the opposite inference from the second half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה stresses 'made for roofing' as the reason the mat is valid. That implies an unlabeled mat is not valid and counts as a mat for lying. So the first half says an unlabeled mat is valid, and the second half says it is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: And then it teaches (in the next clause)
One may roof the סוכה with it
First clause and last clause of a משנה

phrases.english: And then it teaches:
If made for roofing, one may roof with it
and it cannot become impure.
The reason is that he made it for roofing,
which implies that an unspecified mat is for lying on!
phrases.notes: Second inference: this directly contradicts step 13.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction that step 13 began.
steps.kashyaTarget: The status of an unspecified mat (סתמא) in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא implies an unspecified mat is for roofing. The סיפא implies it is for lying. The same משנה cannot say both.

steps.title: Large mat versus small mat
steps.stepSummary: The two halves of the משנה are about different mats. The first half is about a large mat, and the second half is about a small mat.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Here it is talking about a large mat; there it is talking about a small mat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each half of the משנה is about a different size of mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People usually use a large mat for roofing. So an unlabeled large mat is presumed to be for roofing, and only one made for lying is invalid (first half). People usually lie on a small mat. So an unlabeled small mat is presumed to be for lying, and only one made for roofing is valid (second half).

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult (introduces an answer)
Here… there; splits two sources into two different cases
Large (mat)
Small (mat)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the default status of an unlabeled object follows how such objects are normally used.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
here it refers to a large one, there to a small one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּגְדוֹלָה, כָּאן בִּקְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 13–14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each clause is about a different size of mat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses are about the same kind of mat, so their inferences clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Large mat: unlabeled means roofing. Small mat: unlabeled means lying. The two inferences do not clash.

steps.title: The answer works for the חכמים but not for רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The size-based answer fits the חכמים, but רבי אליעזר does not tell small and large mats apart, so the problem comes back for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the רבנן there is no difficulty. But according to רבי אליעזר it is still difficult, as we learned:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a weakness in its own answer and sets up a new challenge. It introduces a quote from רבי אליעזר, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 15 depends on treating small and large mats differently. רבי אליעזר (step 12) says size makes no difference. So for him, the clash between the two inferences seems to come right back.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works fine for…
But (introduces the side where there is still a problem)
The חכמים, the majority view

phrases.english: (Granted, according to the Rabbis it is not difficult;
but according to Rabbi Eliezer it is difficult, as we learned:)

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 15 to the חכמים only.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 15 (large versus small) as applied to רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר treats both sizes the same, so splitting by size cannot remove the contradiction for him.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's words imply an unlabeled mat is for roofing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes רבי אליעזר: for any size, a mat made for lying is invalid. It infers that, in his view, an unlabeled mat of any size is for roofing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: both a small one and a large one, if one made it for lying on, it can become טמא and may not be used as סכך. The reason is that he made it for lying on. That implies a mat made with no stated purpose counts as made for roofing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אליעזר's words as the source for its new challenge. It draws the first inference here; the clashing inference is still to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אליעזר applies this rule to both sizes, the inference 'unlabeled means roofing' holds even for a small mat. This sets up the clash. The size distinction from step 15 cannot be used to escape it.

keyTerms.meaning: Both a small one and a large one: no difference by size

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of step 12. In step 12, רבי אליעזר's view was simply stated. Here the גמרא quotes it again for a new reason: to draw an inference from it and use it in a challenge.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
both a small one and a large one,
if one made it for lying on,
it can become impure, and one may not roof with it.
The reason is that he made it for lying on,
which implies that an unspecified mat is for roofing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַחַת קְטַנָּה וְאַחַת גְּדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source quote that step 16 introduced with 'דִּתְנַן'.
steps.raayaObject: That the contradiction still stands for רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's statement in the משנה: 'אחת קטנה ואחת גדולה, עשאה לשכיבה מקבלת טומאה'
steps.kashyaTarget: The size-based answer of step 15, as applied to רבי אליעזר's statement in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's first clause covers both small and large mats and implies that an unlabeled mat of any size is for roofing. This is the first side of a contradiction that step 18 completes, and a size distinction cannot resolve it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's second clause points the other way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's second clause rules a mat valid only if it was made for roofing. That implies an unlabeled mat is for lying, which clashes with the inference from his first clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now look at the last part of his statement: 'If he made it for roofing, you may roof with it and it cannot become impure.' The reason is that he made it for roofing. So an unlabeled mat must be for lying down!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reads the second half of רבי אליעזר's own words. It shows that this half points the opposite way from the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17, the first clause taught that only a mat made 'for lying' is invalid, so an unlabeled mat is for roofing. Here the second clause stresses 'made for roofing,' which suggests an unlabeled mat is not for roofing but for lying. The earlier size-based answer cannot fix this, because רבי אליעזר applies the same rule to small and large mats.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter clause. The גמרא is turning to the end of the source.
The reason. It introduces a precise inference from the wording.
Unlabeled. Made without any stated purpose.
Ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same contradiction as Steps 13–14. Those were about the חכמים's clauses. Now the contradiction sits inside רבי אליעזר's own statement, so the small-versus-large answer cannot rescue it.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
If he made it for roofing —
one may roof with it
phrases.notes: It is valid as סכך.

phrases.english: and it does not receive impurity.
The reason is that he made it for roofing,
but an unlabeled one — is for lying!
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of the inference drawn in Step 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in Step 17 by setting the סיפא's inference against the רישא's inference.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's statement in the משנה, specifically the earlier size-based resolution as applied to him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two precise inferences from the same speaker's words contradict each other. Since he does not tell sizes apart, the size answer cannot settle it.

steps.title: רבא's new answer: everyone agrees about a large mat
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the earlier answer. He says that for a large mat, all agree an unlabeled one is for roofing. The disagreement is only about a small mat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: about a large mat, everyone agrees that an unlabeled one is for roofing. Where they disagree is about a small mat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא throws out the earlier answer and redraws where the argument lies. Large mats are agreed upon, and the debate is only over small mats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the previous approach is being set aside. Under רבא's reading, the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר agree about large unlabeled mats. That leaves only small mats in dispute, which the next step spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous approach is rejected.
Everyone agrees. Literally, 'all the world does not disagree.'
A large mat / a small mat

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the basic rule: a large unlabeled mat is presumed made for roofing according to everyone.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Regarding a large mat, everyone agrees
that an unlabeled one is for roofing.
Where they disagree is regarding a small mat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the size-based answer of Step 15, which failed for רבי אליעזר in Steps 16–18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the scope of the dispute: agreement on large mats, disagreement only on small mats.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two clauses of the משנה describe different sizes for the חכמים, which leaves רבי אליעזר unexplained.
steps.terutzMaskana: Large unlabeled mats are for roofing according to all. The מחלוקת is limited to small mats.

steps.title: Spelling out the dispute over a small mat
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that an unlabeled small mat is presumed made for lying. רבי אליעזר holds that it too is presumed made for roofing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא holds that an unlabeled small mat is for lying down. רבי אליעזר holds that an unlabeled small mat is also for roofing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by stating each side's view about a small unlabeled mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, a small mat is normally used for lying on, so without a label it is presumed to be for lying and is invalid as סכך. For רבי אליעזר, the word נמי ('also') shows he treats small mats like large ones: unlabeled means for roofing. This fits the inference from his first clause ('whether small or large, if made for lying it is invalid'), which is the reading רבא builds on.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed תנא of the משנה
Holds, is of the opinion
Also, too

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא: an unlabeled large mat is for roofing according to everyone. An unlabeled small mat is for lying according to the תנא קמא, and for roofing according to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
an unlabeled small mat is for lying,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds:
an unlabeled small mat is also for roofing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by stating each opinion about the small mat.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each side a clear presumption for small unlabeled mats.
steps.terutzMaskana: תנא קמא: small unlabeled mat is for lying. רבי אליעזר: small unlabeled mat is also for roofing.
